doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Old styles, big bands and rhythm sections
title: Bix Beiderbecke and Randy Sandke
summary: Pelote defends Bix as the source and praises Randy Sandke's range.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Maybe I’ll take a Bix Beiderbecke record also.

I love Bix. And I guess I would take, oh what’s the one with Bix and his gang. Oh come on Vinny I know it. It’s not “Thou Swell” but it’s one of the Bix and his gang ones. I can’t think of the name now. But I got flak for liking Bix actually.

From people who go like, “What’s so great about Bix?” I mean a lot of modern trumpeters listen to him and they don’t see what the big deal is. And I guess because they’ve heard so many Bix imitators now that they don’t realize that he was the source. It starts with him. Really. They’re all imitating him basically. So it’s like you’ve heard so many of the imitators you can’t appreciate the real thing when you hear it.
Did you ever meet Randy Sandke?

Yes, yes. He brought him to the Institute just recently. Yeah cool Bix. Yeah He’s wild. And there is a case of a guy who, and this is where I think a lot of musicians should sort of follow his lead. I mean he can play the old stuff. But have you heard some of his more out stuff?
Yeah. His writing. Yeah. He did the thing for old time string instruments.
Yeah. He can do the whole gamut. He’s a hell of a musician, definitely is.
